legacy_transcript.json is a normalized transcript of the legacy exec lane (omniview.sdk.exec.v1.ExecPlugin) as SDK v0.21.0 speaks it: the requests, responses and stream frames of the scenario in testdata/compat-v0.21.0/helpers/scenario, as deterministic protobuf bytes (hex, plus a readable rendering). It is not a capture of every wire byte or frame. The recorder re-encodes the decoded protobuf messages, drops empty data frames and groups the remaining stream data by session and target (concatenated). created_at is pinned to the zero Timestamp. A passing replay therefore shows frame-level equality of the messages and of the data per session and target, not equality of every wire byte or of every empty frame: a peer that sends an extra empty data frame still matches.
It was recorded from a real build: a v0.21.0 host (oldhost) talking to a v0.21.0 plugin (oldplugin), built against github.com/omniviewdev/plugin-sdk v0.21.0 = commit ae56fb095c665edc0298c7a7e19cfa8bad8aabca.
TestCompatFramesReplay (pkg/v1/exec/compat_frames_test.go, always on) requires this tree's client and server to reproduce it; TestCompatV0210 (compat_v0210_test.go, CI job with OMNIVIEW_COMPAT_V0210=1) requires a fresh v0.21.0 build to reproduce it, and this tree's host and plugin to match that build.
Do not edit it by hand. Re-recording is for a compatible change of the scenario or of the normalization that this tree's legacy lane and all of T1 to T4 still agree on. It cannot record an intentional change of a recorded legacy reply: T1 still records v0.21.0, T2 then fails the comparison of this tree with it, and record mode leaves the golden unchanged. That is a change of the legacy lane, and it needs its own review and compatibility decision. To re-record: OMNIVIEW_COMPAT_V0210=1 OMNIVIEW_COMPAT_RECORD=1 go test ./pkg/v1/exec/ -run '^TestCompatV0210$' -count=1 -timeout 90m (the golden is written only after the whole matrix, T1 to T4, passed).
To run the real-binary proof without recording: OMNIVIEW_COMPAT_V0210=1 go test ./pkg/v1/exec/ -run '^TestCompatV0210$' -count=1 -v -timeout 90m. Give it the explicit -timeout 90m, as CI does: the fixture commands (module download and the builds of the three helpers) run one after the other and may take longer than go test's default 10 minutes.
OMNIVIEW_COMPAT_SDK_V0210=<dir> builds against a local checkout of the tag instead of downloading it; the checkout must be at commit ae56fb095c665edc0298c7a7e19cfa8bad8aabca with a clean tree (git status --porcelain prints nothing), otherwise the test refuses it; the build then reads a snapshot of that commit (git archive), never the checkout itself, so that no ignored file can change the binaries.
